prompts.spitter_shoot: Use case: identity-preserve. Production transparent game animation sprite sheet. Reference image is the existing ORIGINAL Violet Spitter character identity and rendering style, NOT a pose sequence to copy. Create exactly nine successive frames in a perfectly regular 3 by 3 grid, row-major chronological order. Each equal cell has one complete character of consistent size, looking LEFT in identical three-quarter camera. Preserve teal rounded front armored body, ivory rimmed PURPLE cannon snout, purple rear tank with gold bands, black hoses, four stubby mechanical legs with ivory toes and brass joints, small moss accents. Crisp pixel-art-inspired game sprite styling matching the reference. No text, no lines, no labels, no grid strokes. Genuine transparent background, no ground shadow or ambient glow. Keep all artwork within central 70 percent of each cell, wide transparent gutters, never cross cell edges. Fixed ground contact line at 78 percent of each cell height and body center at 50 percent cell width; identical neutral standing scale across all frames, no camera zoom. Hard clean alpha silhouette, avoid low-opacity haze. Do not add weapons, projectiles, muzzle flash, fire, trails or hit effects. ACTION: a single cannon shooting/recoil cycle. Frame 1 neutral grounded stance matching reference. Frame 2 four feet brace, torso compresses subtly. Frame 3 rear purple pressure tank tenses, cannon pulls back. Frame 4 maximum braced anticipation. Frame 5 the actual release: cannon thrust/recoil with clearly open empty dark muzzle, NO projectile and NO flash. Frame 6 recoil bends front knees. Frame 7 body rebounds. Frame 8 easing back upright. Frame 9 neutral grounded original stance. Retain exactly the same machine in every cell, restrained convincing mechanical action.
